pack.description: Campus and daily-life vocabulary: registration, courses, housing, money and services, as heard in conversations, announcements and emails.
pack.selection_note: Internal high-yield selection of words needed for campus conversations, announcements and emails; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: the university office or official that keeps student records and manages course registration
entries.example_academic: Requests to change a recorded grade must be submitted to the registrar in writing.
entries.example_spoken: You'll have to ask the registrar for an official copy.

entries.definition: a course that a student must complete before being allowed to take another one; something needed first
entries.example_academic: Introductory statistics is a prerequisite for all advanced courses in the department.
entries.example_spoken: I can't take that class yet; I'm missing a prerequisite.

entries.definition: a document that lists the topics, readings, deadlines and rules of a course
entries.example_academic: The syllabus specifies that late work loses ten percent per day.
entries.example_spoken: Check the syllabus; the exam date is on the first page.

entries.definition: an official record of the courses a student has taken and the grades received
entries.example_academic: Applicants must provide an official transcript from each institution attended.
entries.example_spoken: I need to order a transcript for my scholarship application.

entries.definition: the money that students pay for their teaching at a college or university
entries.example_academic: Tuition has risen faster than family incomes for three decades.
entries.example_spoken: My scholarship covers tuition but not housing.

entries.definition: money given to a student, usually because of good results, to help pay for studies
entries.example_academic: The scholarship is awarded on the basis of academic merit rather than financial need.
entries.example_spoken: She got a full scholarship, so she doesn't pay anything.

entries.definition: the latest time or date by which something must be finished or handed in
entries.example_academic: Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.
entries.example_spoken: The deadline is midnight, so we still have three hours.

entries.definition: to officially join a course, school or program
entries.example_academic: Students may enroll in a maximum of eighteen credits per term.
entries.example_spoken: I enrolled in a pottery class just for fun.

entries.definition: one of the two main periods into which the academic year is divided
entries.example_academic: The course is offered only in the spring semester.
entries.example_spoken: This semester is much harder than the last one.

entries.definition: a unit that measures how much work a course is worth toward a degree
entries.example_academic: A minimum of one hundred twenty credits is required for graduation.
entries.example_spoken: I only need three more credits to graduate.

entries.definition: a piece of work that a student is given to do as part of a course
entries.example_academic: Each assignment accounts for ten percent of the final grade.
entries.example_spoken: I still have two assignments due this week.

entries.definition: extra time that is allowed for finishing a piece of work
entries.example_academic: An extension may be granted only in cases of documented illness.
entries.example_spoken: I asked for an extension because I was sick all weekend.

entries.definition: the fixed times each week when a professor is available to meet students without an appointment
entries.example_academic: Students are encouraged to raise individual questions during office hours.
entries.example_spoken: I'll stop by her office hours on Thursday to ask about the essay.

entries.definition: the main subject that a student studies at a college or university
entries.example_academic: Students must declare a major by the end of their second year.
entries.example_spoken: What's your major? Mine is biology.

entries.definition: a student who is studying for a first university degree
entries.example_academic: The laboratory employs several undergraduates as research assistants.
entries.example_spoken: It's unusual for an undergraduate to publish a paper.

entries.definition: all the teachers of a university or of one of its departments
entries.example_academic: The proposal was approved by a vote of the faculty.
entries.example_spoken: Most of the faculty are away at a conference this week.

entries.definition: a member of staff who helps students plan their courses and solve academic problems
entries.example_academic: Each student is assigned an academic advisor in the first term.
entries.example_spoken: My advisor told me not to take five courses.

entries.definition: a building at a college or university where students live
entries.example_academic: First-year students are required to live in a dormitory.
entries.example_spoken: My dormitory is right next to the dining hall.

entries.definition: a person who shares a room or an apartment with you
entries.example_academic: Roommate assignments are announced two weeks before the term begins.
entries.example_spoken: My roommate stays up until three every night.

entries.definition: a legal agreement that allows you to use a house, apartment or car for a period of time in return for payment
entries.example_academic: The lease prohibits tenants from making structural changes.
entries.example_spoken: We signed a twelve-month lease, so we can't leave in May.

entries.definition: a person or company that owns a house or apartment and rents it to others
entries.example_academic: The landlord is responsible for repairs to the heating system.
entries.example_spoken: Our landlord still hasn't fixed the shower.

entries.definition: a person who pays rent to live in a house or apartment or to use land
entries.example_academic: Tenants must give thirty days' notice before leaving.
entries.example_spoken: The previous tenants left the place really clean.

entries.definition: a sum of money that you pay when you rent something and get back if you cause no damage
entries.example_academic: The deposit will be returned within thirty days of the end of the lease.
entries.example_spoken: We lost half our deposit because of the stain on the carpet.

entries.definition: services such as electricity, gas and water that are supplied to a home
entries.example_academic: Rent for university apartments includes all utilities.
entries.example_spoken: Are utilities included, or do we pay them separately?

entries.definition: money that is paid back to you after you have spent your own money on something
entries.example_academic: Requests for reimbursement must include original receipts.
entries.example_spoken: I'm still waiting for my travel reimbursement from the department.

entries.definition: money that is given back to you because you returned something or paid too much
entries.example_academic: A full refund is available until the end of the first week of classes.
entries.example_spoken: I returned the textbook and got a refund.

entries.definition: an amount of money that you pay for a service or to be allowed to do something
entries.example_academic: A late registration fee applies after the first day of classes.
entries.example_spoken: There's a five-dollar fee if you lose your card.

entries.definition: a list of people who are waiting for a place in a course or program that is full
entries.example_academic: Students on the waitlist are admitted in order as places become available.
entries.example_spoken: I'm third on the waitlist, so I might still get in.

entries.definition: a course that a student chooses to take and that is not required for the degree
entries.example_academic: Students complete eight required courses and four electives.
entries.example_spoken: I'm taking photography as an elective.

entries.definition: a period of time during which a student works for an organization in order to gain experience
entries.example_academic: An internship of at least ten weeks is required for the certificate.
entries.example_spoken: I got an internship at a newspaper this summer.

entries.definition: an arrangement to meet someone at a particular time, especially for a professional reason
entries.example_academic: Consultations are by appointment only during the examination period.
entries.example_spoken: I have an appointment with the dentist at four.

entries.definition: a plan that shows when things will happen or when work must be done
entries.example_academic: The construction is proceeding ahead of schedule.
entries.example_spoken: My schedule is packed on Tuesdays.

entries.definition: to travel regularly between home and work or school
entries.example_academic: Nearly half of the students commute from outside the city.
entries.example_spoken: I commute by bike, so I never worry about parking.

entries.definition: a bus or other vehicle that travels regularly between two places
entries.example_academic: A free shuttle connects the main campus with the medical school.
entries.example_spoken: The shuttle runs every twenty minutes until midnight.

entries.definition: a class in which a small group of students discusses a subject with a teacher
entries.example_academic: The seminar is limited to fifteen participants to allow for discussion.
entries.example_spoken: We have to present one article each in the seminar.

entries.definition: a person who gives private or small-group help with a subject
entries.example_academic: Each first-year student is paired with a tutor from the same department.
entries.example_spoken: I found a tutor for statistics through the learning center.

entries.definition: the act of being present at a class or event, or the number of people present
entries.example_academic: Attendance at laboratory sessions is compulsory.
entries.example_spoken: She takes attendance at the start of every class.

entries.definition: the act of using another person's words or ideas as if they were your own
entries.example_academic: Plagiarism is treated as a serious breach of academic integrity.
entries.example_spoken: Copying two sentences without quotation marks counts as plagiarism.

entries.definition: to give a piece of work or a document to someone in authority so that it can be judged or processed
entries.example_academic: All essays must be submitted through the online portal.
entries.example_spoken: I submitted my application five minutes before midnight.

entries.definition: to officially stop taking part in a course; or to take money out of a bank account
entries.translation_fr: se retirer, abandonner (un cours) ; retirer (de l'argent)
entries.example_academic: Students who withdraw after the eighth week receive no refund.
entries.example_spoken: I withdrew from chemistry because I had too much work.

entries.definition: money, such as grants and loans, that helps students pay for their education
entries.example_academic: Financial aid is calculated from the income of the student's family.
entries.example_spoken: Without financial aid, I couldn't afford to study here.

entries.definition: an arrangement in which a student pays in advance for a number of meals in the university dining halls
entries.example_academic: A meal plan is compulsory for students living in university housing.
entries.example_spoken: My meal plan runs out next week, so I'll be cooking.

entries.definition: a program of information and activities that introduces new students or employees to a place
entries.example_academic: Orientation for international students takes place a week before classes begin.
entries.example_spoken: I met most of my friends during orientation.

entries.definition: a meeting in which people learn about a subject by discussing it and doing practical exercises
entries.example_academic: The writing center offers a workshop on citation practices each term.
entries.example_spoken: There's a workshop on interview skills tomorrow at five.

entries.definition: a printed sheet of information given to people at a class or meeting
entries.example_academic: The handout summarizes the main stages of the experiment.
entries.example_spoken: Did you get the handout from Monday's class?

entries.definition: an examination taken in the middle of a school term
entries.example_academic: The midterm covers the material from the first six weeks.
entries.example_spoken: I have two midterms on the same day.

entries.definition: the qualification that a student receives after completing a course of study at a university
entries.example_academic: The degree requires four years of full-time study.
entries.example_spoken: He has a degree in engineering but works as a chef.

entries.definition: houses, apartments and rooms for people to live in, or the job of providing them
entries.example_academic: Demand for student housing exceeds supply in most university towns.
entries.example_spoken: I'm still looking for housing for next year.

entries.definition: a written order from a doctor for a medicine
entries.example_academic: Antibiotics are available only with a prescription.
entries.example_spoken: I need to pick up my prescription before the pharmacy closes.

entries.definition: an arrangement in which you pay a company regularly and it pays the costs if you are ill, have an accident or lose something
entries.example_academic: International students are required to hold health insurance.
entries.example_spoken: Does your insurance cover dental work?

entries.definition: paid work that takes up only part of the normal working week
entries.translation_fr: emploi à temps partiel, petit boulot
entries.example_academic: Students who hold a part-time job tend to manage their time more carefully.
entries.example_spoken: I have a part-time job at the campus bookstore.

entries.definition: one of the periods into which the working day is divided, or the group of people working then
entries.example_academic: Nurses on the night shift reported higher levels of fatigue.
entries.example_spoken: I can't come; I have a shift at the café until nine.

entries.definition: not done, paid or returned by the expected time
entries.example_academic: Fines are charged on overdue books at a daily rate.
entries.example_spoken: My library book is two weeks overdue.

entries.definition: to make something valid for a further period of time
entries.example_academic: Loans may be renewed twice unless another reader has requested the item.
entries.example_spoken: I need to renew my parking permit before Friday.

entries.definition: an amount of money that you borrow and must pay back, usually with extra money for the cost of borrowing
entries.example_academic: Graduates begin repaying their loans six months after leaving university.
entries.example_spoken: I took out a loan to pay for my last year.

entries.definition: required by a rule or law
entries.example_academic: Safety training is mandatory for anyone working in the laboratory.
entries.example_spoken: The Friday session isn't mandatory, but you should go.

entries.definition: allowed to do or receive something because you meet the conditions
entries.example_academic: Only full-time students are eligible for the grant.
entries.example_spoken: Am I eligible for the discount if I'm a part-time student?

entries.definition: to decide officially that a rule, fee or right will not be applied
entries.translation_fr: renoncer à, dispenser de, supprimer (des frais)
entries.example_academic: The department may waive the requirement for students with relevant experience.
entries.example_spoken: They waived the late fee because it was my first time.

entries.definition: to rent to another person a room or apartment that you yourself are renting
entries.example_academic: Tenants may not sublet the property without written permission.
entries.example_spoken: I'm subletting my room for the summer while I'm away.

entries.definition: a long piece of writing on a subject, done as part of an advanced university degree
entries.example_academic: Her dissertation examines trade networks in the medieval Mediterranean.
entries.example_spoken: He's been writing his dissertation for three years.

entries.definition: a fixed amount of money that is paid regularly to a student or researcher to cover living costs
entries.example_academic: Doctoral students receive a monthly stipend in addition to free tuition.
entries.example_spoken: The stipend is small, but it covers rent.

entries.definition: the right of a professor to keep a teaching job permanently
entries.example_academic: Tenure protects scholars who pursue unpopular lines of research.
entries.example_spoken: She's up for tenure next year, so she's publishing a lot.

entries.definition: to attend a course without receiving a grade or credit for it; or to examine accounts officially
entries.translation_fr: suivre en auditeur libre ; vérifier (des comptes)
entries.example_academic: Members of the public may audit lectures with the instructor's consent.
entries.example_spoken: I'm auditing a history class just because I like the professor.

entries.definition: a ceremony at which students formally receive their degrees
entries.example_academic: Commencement will be held outdoors unless heavy rain is forecast.
entries.example_spoken: My whole family is flying in for commencement.

entries.definition: a former student of a school, college or university
entries.example_academic: The new library was financed largely by donations from alumni.
entries.example_spoken: He's an alumnus of this department, class of 2010.

entries.definition: a person who watches students during an examination to make sure the rules are followed
entries.example_academic: A proctor will verify each candidate's identity before the test begins.
entries.example_spoken: The proctor took his phone away during the exam.

entries.definition: a period of paid leave given to a university teacher for study or travel
entries.example_academic: She completed the book during a sabbatical at a research institute abroad.
entries.example_spoken: Professor Lee is on sabbatical this year, so someone else teaches the course.

entries.definition: official approval given to a school or program that meets required standards
entries.example_academic: The program lost its accreditation after failing two consecutive reviews.
entries.example_spoken: Check that the online school has accreditation before you pay.

entries.definition: a senior official at a university who is in charge of its academic programs
entries.translation_fr: vice-président aux affaires académiques, recteur adjoint
entries.example_academic: The provost announced a review of all graduate programs.
entries.example_spoken: The petition has to go to the provost, not the dean.

entries.definition: the official at a college or university who is responsible for money, especially student payments
entries.example_academic: Outstanding balances must be settled with the bursar before graduation.
entries.example_spoken: Go to the bursar if you think you were charged twice.
